candidate.subject: One account, more podcasts
candidate.preview_text: Add podcasts without a separate charge for creating each one.
candidate.headline: Host multiple shows in one account
candidate.body:
When a new client or internal podcast needs a host, you can place it in the same Transistor account as your other shows. A paid account does not add a separate charge for creating each additional podcast.

Transistor is a podcast hosting platform for carrying multiple shows in one account. From there, distribute each podcast to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube, Overcast, Pocket Casts and more.

Use that account for the podcasts your agency produces, then publish each one to the listening apps its audience uses.

The free trial runs for 14 days, giving you a defined window to decide whether Transistor fits the hosting plan for your next show.

During the free trial, you can host multiple client podcasts in the same account.

issues.detail: "During the free trial, you can host multiple client podcasts in the same account.": The sources separately document a 14-day trial and multi-podcast hosting, but do not establish that multi-podcast creation or hosting is available during the trial. Combining those facts does not prove trial feature access.
No supplied source establishes that the documented multi-podcast capability is available during the free trial.
This directly violates the campaign instruction: “Do not claim that multi-show creation or distribution is available during the trial.”

decision.summary: The core multi-show, no-extra-per-podcast-charge, distribution, and 14-day-trial claims are supported. Revision is required because the draft additionally promises multi-podcast hosting during the trial, which is neither sourced nor permitted by the instructions.

benefit_retention.explanation: The draft retains the supported core benefit: agencies can create additional podcasts in one Transistor account without an extra per-podcast charge and distribute them to major listening apps.
